subject: MedTech Co — post-demo: SDK/auth/routing + policy next steps

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: MedTech co — post-demo recap & immediate asks (SDK/auth/routing)

Hi Samira — thanks again for a great call today. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we stay coordinated across product, infra, and your platform team.

Call summary (30-min demo + Qs)
- Goal: replace existing on-prem LLM routing with a hybrid approach (private VPC for PHI-sensitive calls, hosted for lower-sensitivity inference).
- Primary workloads: clinical note summarization (structured output + tool calling), patient Q&A (dialogue + embeddings for search), and batch reranking for clinical search.
- Latency target: ~250ms p95 for 256-512 token generations in steady state (you flagged 300ms p95 as max).

Immediate technical asks (what we promised to follow up)
1) SDK & language: you said engineering is Python-first (FastAPI + k8s). We'll provide a Python SDK quickstart. Please confirm if Go is needed.
2) Auth model: you asked about mTLS and API key options. We support API key + region pinning and Private with mutual-TLS in Private deployments. Need to confirm whether MedTech will require HSM-backed key management or mTLS for all traffic.
3) Routing & policy: draft proposal: primary route to a high-performance quantized model for low-latency; fallback chain to smaller models when capacity constrained; region routing (US east primary, EU as failover for DR). We will send a sample routing_policy YAML.
4) Structured output & tool-calling: for summaries we propose structured JSON schema enforcement + tool calling for record lookups. We'll link an example output schema and a sample OpenAPI tool spec.
5) Embeddings / reranker: recommendation: 1536-d dense embeddings, vector DB in your VPC (we can push embed ops to Private), and a pairwise reranker (small transformer) that runs as a low-latency scoring stage.

Attachments: integration guide and schema mapping (attached) — the integration guide has the Python SDK quickstart and auth examples.

Next steps / proposed timeline
- Today / tomorrow: confirm mTLS vs API key requirement and whether Go SDK needed.
- By EOD Thu: internal tech kickoff (we'll loop infra and product).
- Next week: PoC plan (2-week bench + sample dataset) to validate p95 latency and fallback behavior.

HubSpot: I added the call notes to our deal record: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567

Let me know any clarifications or if I missed anything. Happy to jump back on a quick 20-min call with engineering next week.

— Alex

Thanks Alex — that matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- SDK language: Python is sufficient for the initial PoC; Go might be useful later but not required for the trial.
- Auth: Security wants mTLS on Private endpoints and API keys for hosted with IP allowlists. HSM-backed keys are preferred for production. Can you confirm Redwood supports KMS/HSM integrations for Private?
- Latency: our SKUs must meet <=300ms p95 for 512 tokens; 250ms p95 would be ideal. We also need a cold-start behavior note — how the KV cache warms and how it affects p95.
- Data flow: for PHI-sensitive traffic we require requests to stay within our VPC and audit logs streamed to our SIEM.

Attached: a short schema sample and a list of 200 representative queries for initial bench.

Can we give engineering next Wed (Aug 18) for a deep technical sync? Prefer 10–11AM PT.

— Samira

Team — forwarding Samira's reply. Core asks are mTLS for Private, API keys + IP allowlist for hosted, HSM for prod keys, latency SLO ~250–300ms p95, and audit log streaming. Please see action items and owners below.

Engineering asks (please reply with owners & ETA):
1) SDK quickstart (Python) + example FastAPI integration, auth examples (API key, client cert mTLS). Owner: Dev? ETA: 3 business days for sample repo.
2) Private deployment auth & KMS/HSM notes: can we support mutual TLS and HSM key wrapping in our Private offering? If not fully supported, what are the gaps and mitigation steps. Owner: Karthik.
3) Routing policy & fallback chain: draft a routing_policy_draft.yaml that captures:
   - primary model: redwood-azimuth-13b-quant (us-east) for low-latency
   - fallback_1: redwood-aurora-7b-quant (us-east, lower cost)
   - fallback_2: redwood-azimuth-13b-quant (eu-west) when us capacity constrained for DR (only for non-PHI calls)
   - policy rules: prefer latency policy up to p95=250ms, cost throttles when token budget exceeds threshold, separate policy for PHI to force Private-only route
   - KV cache: prefix caching (30m TTL) and per-customer cache namespace
4) Latency bench: run a PoC with the 200 representative queries Samira attached and report p50/p95/p99 for 256/512 token distributions. Also measure cold-start impact. Owner: Marissa.
5) Embeddings & reranker: propose embed dimensionality (1536) and an architecture diagram where embedding ops can be pushed into customer VPC for PHI. Reranker should be an additional scoring pass (pairwise) — include expected extra latency. Owner: Dev + Karthik.

Notes & constraints:
- For PHI-sensitive requests we must not route to eu-west (privacy + GDPR complications) — enforce via routing_policy tags.
- Samira asked for audit log streaming — we support streaming Syslog/S3 connectors; check retention SLA.
- DocuSign / legal: Samira mentioned an internal review; we should prepare a short security appendix for their InfoSec.

I attached our integration guide and the initial mapping sheet. I sketched a sample YAML for the routing policy in the attached routing_policy_draft.yaml — please iterate.

Thanks — can you each reply by EOD with owners and a one-sentence ETA? I’ll lock the deep tech sync for Aug 18 10AM PT if that works.

— Alex

All — quick status and proposed next steps.

Owners / ETAs:
- Dev Patel: SDK quickstart (Python) + FastAPI example + auth snippets (API key + mTLS example). ETA: 72 hours (EOD Mon Aug 17).
- Karthik Iyer: Routing policy YAML draft and service-level rules (PHI tag enforcement, region routing, fallback chain). Will include a short note on how to wire KV cache namespaces. ETA: 48 hours (EOD Fri Aug 15).
- Marissa (me): PoC bench with 200 queries; will run on Dedicated capacity in us-east to measure p50/p95/p99 for 256/512 token shapes and cold-start. ETA: initial results by Wed Aug 19 COB.

Quick technical notes for policy draft (to be included in routing_policy_draft.yaml):
- default_route: redwood-azimuth-13b-quant@us-east
- fallbacks:
  - redwood-aurora-7b-quant@us-east (lower-cost, lower-context)
  - redwood-azimuth-13b-quant@eu-west (DR-only, non-PHI)
- policies:
  - name: latency-first
    criteria: p95 <= 250ms
    action: route_to_primary
  - name: cost-throttle
    criteria: tokens_per_minute > 250k
    action: prefer_fallbacks
  - name: phi-enforce-private
    criteria: request.tag == PHI
    action: force_private_vpc
- cache:
  - kv_cache_ttl: 1800 # seconds (30m)
  - cache_namespace: customer_medtechco

Auth notes: we support API keys for hosted + IP allowlist; Private supports mutual TLS and can integrate with customer KMS for key encryption (we’ll document HSM workflows in the security appendix). Karthik, please confirm the HSM/KMS integration specifics for Private deployment.

Embeddings & reranker:
- Recommend 1536-d embeddings (we have test profiles).
- Reranker: two-pass model (fast embed + pairwise reranker). Expect +10–40ms per query depending on batch size and model choice — include as config option in policy.

Next meeting: confirm Aug 18 10–11AM PT for deep technical sync (I’ve tentatively added a calendar invite).
